{{Quote|It is said that for over ten thousand years the ancient citadel of Ebenmal had never fallen before an invader. It took one night and a single company of Imperial jumptroopers to wipe away that particular distinction.|[[Chen Ming-di]]|<ref name="TFU II" />}}
'''Jumptroopers''', otherwise known as '''skytroopers''', '''rocket troopers''', or '''air assault troopers''', were a variant of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] trained in airborne environments such as [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], or assigned to battlefields with treacherous terrain. They were heavily armed with various [[Projectile launcher/Legends|projectile launchers]] or [[Heavy blaster rifle/Legends|heavy blaster rifles]].

They drew inspiration from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Rocket-Jumper Elite Advance Unit]], an elite soldier trained in the use of airborne assaults, or the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic's]] [[Clone jet trooper/Legends|Clone Jet Troopers]]. Decades after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], they continued to be used by [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon's]] [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]].

==Overview==
The jumptroopers were an air-to-ground attack unit that was trained to engage airborne, entrenched, or otherwise inaccessible enemies. They were also trained in hit-and-run attacks in which they ambushed the enemy from above. They often provided stormtrooper units with air cover during pitched battles.<ref name="Commander's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> They were the primary Imperial unit designated to "keep order" on low-gravity worlds or on atmospheric platforms such as [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="TFU" />

==Equipment==
Many of these soldiers wore specialized [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|stormtrooper armor]] with breathing hoses attached to the chest unit and a helmet similar to that worn by [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|CC-2224]]. Some jumptroopers wore stormtrooper armor with red decals painted on, along with black shoulder pads and what appeared to be [[Clone trooper armor/Legends|clone trooper chest plates]]. Furthermore, the forehead of this helmet was shaped in a black "v" and had a single red line on it with two red lights by the chin. Later troopers would wear more bulky armor.<ref name="TFU" />

[[File:Merr-sonnJT-12ImperialJetpack.jpg|thumb|left|100px|A [[JT-12 jetpack/Legends|JT-12 jetpack]] used by some Imperial jumptroopers.]]

They could use [[jump pack]]s or [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpacks]]. Notably, they used [[Hush-About AJP-400|AJP-400 Jet Packs]] or [[JT-12 jetpack/Legends|JT-12 Jetpacks]]. The [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn]] had missile systems integrated in their jetpacks, that when it exploded, acted like a [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]].<ref name="Commander's Guide" />

[[File:Rocket_trooper.jpg|thumb|right|160px|Rocket Troopers serving the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]]]

Jumptroopers employed various types of [[Projectile launcher/Legends|projectile launchers]] and [[Heavy blaster rifle/Legends|heavy blaster rifles]]. Jumptroopers were known to wield [[plasma caster]]s, long-range [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrowers]]. While some used [[rail detonator]]s or anti-infantry [[Flechette/Legends|flechette]] canisters. Some could carry [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launchers]]. They were armed with [[Plasma disruptor/Legends|plasma disruptors]], which were far more powerful than standard Imperial-issued weaponry and were noted for their lack of a recoil. Thus the jumptroopers could discharge the weapon's fiery white bolts without changing their flight path or being knocked off balance while flying. This allowed them to seek a high vantage point in the air and take out their foes at a distance. Besides this, they were occasionally outfitted with rocket launchers.<ref name="Commander's Guide" />

==History==
These troopers were stationed on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], and the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. On [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]], jumptroopers were part of the garrison guarding the [[Imperial Ore Facility]]. They engaged in numerous battles against [[Galen Marek]], who came by the planets on which they were stationed.<ref name="TFU" />

[[File:Jumptrooper_Starkiller.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Subject 1138|Starkiller]] attacks a jumptrooper on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].]]

A number of jumptroopers were stationed on the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], where they attempted to stop the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Subject 1138|test subject]] of the [[Death/Legends|deceased]] Starkiller. Despite their best efforts, the clone easily defeated them all and [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escaped]] the planet. Later, they [[Rescue of Rahm Kota|fought]] the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] on [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]] under [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] of [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]] in the city of [[Tarko-se/Legends|Tarko-se]]. He killed them all. When the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Assault on Kamino|attacked]] Kamino, the clone encountered and killed them also.<ref name="TFU II" />

Several were under the command of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] to [[Raid at Spaceport THX1138|capture]] a [[Unidentified Rebel spy|rebel agent]] aboard one of the [[StarSpeeder 1000]]s.<ref name="ST2">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref>

Jumptroopers were later assigned to protect the [[Thundering Herd/Legends|Thundering Herd's]] [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transports]] during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. Some of these airtroopers also accompanied Darth Vader during his attempt to [[Occupation of Bespin|capture]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="SSW" />

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], rocket troopers were still in service and assisted the [[Disciples of Ragnos]], a shadowy cult that had intentions in reviving the ancient deceased [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Marka Ragnos]]. They fought [[Jaden Korr]] [[Mission to Taspir III|at]] [[Taspir III]]. In the end, the [[Disciples of Ragnos crisis|attempt]] to resurrect Ragnos failed during the [[Battle of Korriban (Disciples of Ragnos crisis)|Battle of]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="Jedi Academy" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:ImperialJumptrooperAlternate-TFU.png|thumb|right|150px|An Imperial Jet Trooper as seen in {{TFU|version=PSP, PS2 and Wii}}]]
''[[Super Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' featured airtroopers as one of its many enemies. Their designation as air assault troopers was later revealed in [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 4|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 4]].

The Hasbro jumptrooper toy's design was based on the unit in the PS3 and Xbox 360 versions of the game, as it possessed a hose connecting the helmet to a breathing tank on the chest armor. The version in the PS2, PSP, and Wii ports looked more like a standard stormtrooper with heavy shoulder armor. The figure's bio also stated that they were equipped with rail detonators, though these do not feature in the game. The title of "jumptrooper" comes from [[Hasbro]] toy catalogs and does not feature a jetpack.

The jumptrooper is called the [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]] Trooper in the ''Star Wars Miniatures'' game.
